summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of kidney transplant, coronary artery disease, and multiple comorbidities, was admitted for non-infectious diarrhea with 10 watery bowel movements per day and associated weakness and shortness of breath. She had recently been hospitalized for acute kidney injury attributed to opioid use and dehydration. Admission labs showed elevated creatinine at 3.1, consistent with acute on chronic kidney disease. Stool studies, including C. difficile PCR, cultures, ova and parasites, and CMV viral load, were negative. Renal function improved with IV fluids and holding Lasix temporarily. Diarrhea resolved with loperamide. Tacrolimus was increased to 2 mg twice daily to ensure adequate immunosuppression. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for outpatient GI follow-up and continued management of her transplant and chronic conditions.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Adverse effect of antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs, initial encounter
